requirement_text.REQ-050: Port src/engine/transition.zig's EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY branch (per src/design/engine.md "Section EE-05: Exclusive Gateway/CEL", L2238) into REQ-044's transition dispatch. Pure, no I/O, same contract as REQ-044. - Outgoing edge conditions are evaluated in DECLARED edge order and the token follows the FIRST edge whose condition evaluates true (EE-05 AC1). - An edge with is_default true is evaluated LAST regardless of its declared position, and carries no condition expression (EE-05 AC2). REQ-029 already enforces at definition time that is_default and a non-null condition cannot coexist and that at most one default edge exists per gateway, so this requirement may rely on those invariants rather than re-validating them -- state that reliance explicitly. - Exactly one outgoing edge is followed per evaluation: never zero, never more than one (EE-05 AC5). - A condition that raises a runtime error (type mismatch, undefined variable) is treated as FALSE for that edge, not as an instance error (EE-05 AC4 and its edge case). This is easy to get backwards -- a condition erroring is different from no condition matching. - If no condition matches and no default edge exists, the instance transitions to ERROR per REQ-061's EE-10 path, with a structured reason naming the gateway node_id and the conditions that were evaluated (EE-05 AC3). The reason must carry enough detail for an operator to diagnose without replaying (EE-10 AC5), so record the evaluated conditions, not just the node id. CONDITION EVALUATION -- port against R-Co's real, working implementation, which is NOT vendor/cel/cel.zig. Read src/engine/transition.zig's evaluateGatewayCondition() (~line 1118, R-Co's EXP-102 adapter) as the reference: it translates the CEL-syntax condition string stored in definition graphs into expr syntax, then parses and evaluates via R-Co's src/expr/ module (7 files: lexer.zig, parser.zig, ast.zig, evaluator.zig, error.zig, mod.zig, benchmark.zig). Its own header states the contract this requirement needs: "Returns false on any translation, parse, or evaluation error -- preserving the same `catch false` semantics as the previous cel.evaluate call," plus an explicit I/O-free guarantee ("expr.parse() and expr.evaluate() are pure computations"), which is exactly what REQ-044's purity contract requires. That catch-false rule IS EE-05 AC4's treat-errors-as-false behaviour -- port it as one rule, not two. The translation layer (translateCelToExpr) is small and fully specified in transition.zig: strip the `variables.` prefix, map `&&`->`and`, `||`->`or`, `!`->`not ` (with `!=` passing through unchanged), and return no-match for expressions using unsupported CEL features (macros, type-conversion functions, collection functions, the ternary operator) -- which, via catch-false, means those conditions evaluate false rather than erroring the instance. Port that supported/unsupported boundary explicitly rather than inferring it, and cite hasCelUnsupportedFeatures() as its source. Note on a stale citation, so it is not re-propagated: REQ-029's description states R-Co's vendor/cel/cel.zig is a stub. That wording comes from src/design/definition.md (and engine.md's own EE-05 section, lines 451/1005/1020, which the code has since superseded) and was correct for REQ-029's own scope -- DEFINITION-TIME syntax checking, where Letflow indeed ships only isValidCelSyntax with no evaluation. It does NOT describe runtime evaluation today: R-Co commit 480b7dc5 wired src/expr into transition.zig and retired vendor/cel from production, and vendor/cel/cel.zig is in any case a real 13,877-byte subset evaluator with a working evaluate() at line 391, not a stub. This requirement therefore has a real reference implementation to port and needs no build-vs-adopt decision record. Whatever lands must stay deterministic and I/O-free to preserve REQ-044's purity contract. SCOPE NOTE: R-Co reaches src/expr/ as a named module shared beyond the engine. Letflow has no expression evaluator yet, so this requirement builds the minimal evaluator the gateway path actually needs (the operators and comparisons translateCelToExpr can produce), not a port of all 7 src/expr/ files -- benchmark.zig in particular is a Zig benchmarking harness with no Elixir equivalent here. State in the moduledoc which subset landed and that a fuller expression surface, if a later stage needs one, extends this rather than replacing it. CLARIFICATION FROM ORCH (dependency check, not in the original requirement text): REQ-050's depends_on lists only REQ-044, not REQ-061 -- this is correct, not an oversight. REQ-061 (execution error handling, EE-10) is still `pending`/not yet built. lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex's existing contract (REQ-044, already shipped) is `transition/3` returning `{:ok, ...} | {:error, transition_error()}` tagged tuples -- e.g. the existing stub `dispatch_exclusive_gateway/4` at transition.ex:256-259 already returns `{:error, {:gateway_not_yet_implemented, :EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY, node_id}}`. 'The instance transitions to ERROR' for this requirement's purposes means: this pure module returns a distinctly-tagged `{:error, {:no_matching_edge, node_id, evaluated_conditions}}`-shaped tuple (exact shape is this design's own call) following the same `transition_error()` type-union pattern already established -- it does NOT mean calling into REQ-061 code, which doesn't exist yet. REQ-061/REQ-045's future orchestration layer is what will later interpret this tuple and actually mark an instance ERROR in the DB; that is out of this requirement's scope. NOTE ON SOURCE ACCESS: the R-Co source checkout (c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\R-Co\) is not present on this host (~/letflow only, no sibling R-Co directory) -- do not spend time searching for src/engine/transition.zig or src/expr/ on disk here, they don't exist in this environment. Work from the requirement text's own inline specification above, which already restates every rule this design needs (the four translateCelToExpr rewrites, the catch-false semantics, the unsupported-feature boundary) verbatim from the Zig source. This matches how REQ-044/063/064 were designed and shipped from this same host without R-Co access.

task.description: Design the EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY branch of Letflow.Engine.Transition's dispatch (replacing the dispatch_exclusive_gateway/4 stub at transition.ex:256-259) plus a new minimal pure CEL-subset expression evaluator module (e.g. Letflow.Engine.Expr or similar -- name it in the design) that the gateway dispatch calls to evaluate each outgoing edge's condition string. Read lib/letflow/design/req044-transition-kernel.md first for the established conventions (purity contract, transition_error() type union, dispatch_*/4 function shape, moduledoc style) and match them. Write lib/letflow/design/req050-exclusive-gateway-cel.md per Step 1's standard shape: public function signatures with @spec-style types, key data structures, invariants, DB touched (none -- this stays pure per REQ-044's contract), cross-module deps, and open questions. Design must cover: edge evaluation in declared order with default-last; the exact evaluated-conditions data recorded in the no-match error tuple; the translateCelToExpr rewrite rules (variables. prefix strip, && -> and, || -> or, ! -> not with != passing through) and where that translation lives (same module as evaluation, or a separate step); the supported/unsupported CEL feature boundary (macros, type-conversion functions, collection functions, ternary operator all treated as no-match/false); and the catch-false semantics applied uniformly to translation, parse, and evaluation errors alike.
acceptance_criteria: a gateway whose second declared edge is the first to evaluate true routes the token down that edge, not the first or third -- an explicit ordering test, not a single-edge case

a gateway with a default edge declared FIRST and two non-default edges that both evaluate false routes the token down the default edge, proving the default is evaluated last regardless of declared position

a condition expression that raises a runtime error (undefined variable or type mismatch) is treated as false and evaluation continues to the next edge, rather than transitioning the instance to ERROR -- an explicit test distinguishing this from the no-match case
a gateway where no condition matches and no default edge exists transitions the instance to ERROR with a structured reason naming the gateway node_id AND the conditions that were evaluated
exactly one outgoing edge is followed in every passing case, asserted directly rather than inferred

a condition using an unsupported CEL feature (a macro, a type-conversion function, a collection function, or the ternary operator) evaluates to false via the catch-false rule rather than raising or erroring the instance, matching hasCelUnsupportedFeatures()'s boundary -- at least two such expressions tested explicitly

the CEL-to-expr translation is tested directly on each of its four documented rewrites (variables. prefix stripped, && -> and, || -> or, ! -> not with != passing through unchanged), rather than only end-to-end through gateway evaluation

the evaluator performs zero I/O and is deterministic, confirmed by inspection of its call graph and stated in the moduledoc, which cites src/engine/transition.zig's evaluateGatewayCondition() and src/expr/ as the ported reference and records which subset of the expression surface landed

result.summary: Wrote lib/letflow/design/req050-exclusive-gateway-cel.md, replacing REQ-044's dispatch_exclusive_gateway/4 stub with a full design: the new @spec returning {:ok, InstanceState.t(), []} | {:error, {:no_matching_edge, node_id, evaluated_conditions}}, a new pure module Letflow.Engine.Expr (lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex) with translate_cel_to_expr/1, parse/1, eval/2, and the composed catch-false entry point evaluate_condition/2, an internal expr-AST type covering variable refs/comparisons/and/or/not/literals, the 4 exact translateCelToExpr rewrite rules (variables. prefix strip, && -> and, || -> or, ! -> not with != passing through) with the !=-carve-out flagged as load-bearing, the supported/unsupported CEL feature boundary (macros, type-conversion functions, collection functions, ternary) ported from hasCelUnsupportedFeatures(), the uniform catch-false rule folding translation/parse/eval errors into one boolean-false outcome, the declared-order first-true-wins default-last edge-selection algorithm (default edge structurally excluded from the ordering loop, evaluated unconditionally last), the extended transition_error() with a new evaluated_condition() type naming edge_id/condition/result per evaluated edge, explicit reliance on REQ-029's CHK-13..CHK-16 invariants (default/condition mutual exclusivity, at most one default edge) stated as relied-upon not re-validated, the purity/determinism verification method matching REQ-044's own grep/mix xref pattern, and 4 explicit open questions (unsupported-feature detection mechanism, a defensive :translate_error addition, the zero-outgoing-edge degenerate case, and mismatched-type equality comparison semantics). All 8 acceptance criteria are traced to concrete design elements in section 10's table.
